subject: Business Models
title: Insurance Origins
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Insurance Origins.

hook.text: Sending a ship across the ocean was hugely profitable—if it survived. Many didn't.

buildup.text: Merchants needed a way to share the risk. If one ship sank, they couldn't lose everything.

discovery.text: Lloyd's Coffee House in London became the center of marine insurance in the 1680s.

twist.text: Lloyd's wasn't a company—it was a marketplace where individuals bet on ships surviving voyages.

climax.text: Insurance made global trade scalable. Without risk-sharing, only the richest could afford commerce.

punchline.text: Global trade runs on managed risk. Insurance made it safe.

details.summary: Insurance originated in maritime trade when merchants pooled risk by spreading cargo across multiple ships or paying others to bear the risk of loss. Lloyd's of London evolved from a 17th century coffee house where ship owners, merchants, and underwriters met to negotiate marine insurance contracts.
details.whyItMatters: Insurance enabled commerce by making catastrophic risk manageable. Without insurance, few merchants would risk valuable cargo on dangerous voyages..
takeaways: Merchants spread cargo across multiple ships to reduce total loss risk on any single voyage
Lloyd's of London evolved from a coffee house where marine insurance was negotiated
Risk pooling and transfer enabled merchants to undertake previously dangerous ventures

faq.question: How did early marine insurance work?
faq.answer: A merchant paid a premium to an underwriter who agreed to cover losses if the ship sank or cargo was damaged. The underwriter literally wrote their name under the risk description, hence the term. Premiums varied based on route danger, cargo value, ship condition, and captain reputation.

faq.question: How did Lloyd's coffee house become a global insurance market?
faq.answer: Edward Lloyd's coffee house in the 1680s attracted ship captains, merchants, and wealthy individuals willing to underwrite risk. The concentrated market made it efficient to negotiate insurance..
